analysis.title: GS Materials - Nov 19. Copper - Positioning, Supply v Demand, Left hand v Right hand and the biggest question of all. WEBCAST REPLAY
key_insights: Author James McGeoch (GS FICC and Equities desk, not Global Investment Research) says the market moved first and asked questions later on 11/18. He calls it a Covid/Liberation day type move on no news and disagrees that dollar availability explains the caution, citing a >$100bn IPO raise the same day.

US and China each hold a lever: the US has copper and China has rare earths. The author says the market priced that the US would not tariff copper, which would imply China would not impose a rare earth export ban (Jan 11 deadline). He is unsure what Trump's comment that the US has a rare earth solution means for the copper tariff.

Negative import arbitrage (very large China physical premiums) means the US stops importing copper as early as December. CESCO says more than 100kt could be re-exported in December, with November still near 200kt. The open question is how fast exports run.

On the question of peak US rate hawkishness, most webcast participants said yes. The author argues that if you are at peak hawkishness you go to gold first, usually through baskets such as GSXGGLDM before single stocks. He also notes a filing showing Druckenmiller buying gold and reasons that he likely bought back the copper he had sold.

Positioning: the GS commodities desk thinks the macro franchise held a 5/10 short via options coming into the week, and Chinese shorts on SHFE are approaching local highs. The author says the market has been long or flat copper for two years, so it has room to add. China added to Shanghai shorts on the day and sold everything on Monday, with an unverified rumor of A-share short sale restrictions around the APEC summit pushing flow into commodities.

Supply is a main question. The author says GS supply estimates contain nothing overly ambitious and a series of company updates is due: BHP next week, Glencore a couple of weeks later, Vale after Thanksgiving and an expected Rio update.

China end demand remains negative while apparent demand is propped up by scrap tightness. Scrap lost about 600kt of metal and could reach 1mt by year end under the reverse invoice policy. GS is watching whether the tax bureau steps back or supply chain models shift, and has seen neither.

China end use demand is running about -2-3% y/y, or 500kt. Power equipment is the only bright spot. Air conditioner demand went from flat in 1Q to -10% (over 15% of China copper use), and State Grid copper consumption is negative y/y. The author calls the weakness cyclical, sees possible acceleration into year end and thinks 2027 can be less negative.

BHP Copper South Australia day on Nov 23 covers the Phase 1 expansion to about 500ktpa. Phase 1 is already in GS base case forecasts and is about one third of BHP's long run 3-4% Cu Eq growth target. GS watches capex (last estimate US$10-11.6bn vs GS ~US$11bn), costs, returns, smelter design, block cave risk and uranium recovery.

GS computes BHP free cash flow for FY27/28/29 after dividends and equity investments (including Vicuna and South Australia copper) that is negative or near zero at iron ore of $95, $85 and $75. The author says leverage will need modelling and notes BHP has sold some infrastructure and streaming interests to fund this period.
Glencore has bought about 58% of its $500m buyback as the share price fell. The author is tracking how stocks respond to the lower copper price.

Chile and Codelco: client discussions point to the cost of saving El Teniente and a possible sale of El Abra. The author contrasts Australia with Chile on incentives to invest and lists vicuna, South Australia, Arizona, DRC and Chile as copper growth options.
GS 2027 outlook pieces are linked, including an iron ore 2027 forecast cut to about US$90/t. A Commodity Outlook webinar with Daan Struyven is scheduled for the next day.

market_movers.rationale: Copper South Australia day on Nov 23. GS models Phase 1 at about 20% IRR at its long run copper price and about 15% at consensus prices, and sees negative to near zero FCF through FY29 at current iron ore.
Named as one of three single stocks with a CMD style update expected after Thanksgiving.
The author expects an update from Rio that he has not yet seen. Rio's JV with Codelco was also discussed.
Glencore has bought about 58% of its $500m buyback and has an update expected in early December.

sector_views.rationale: Positioning is described as long or flat with room to add and supply updates are due, but China end demand is negative and FCF at BHP is stretched at current iron ore prices. The author is less worried about copper medium to long term.

earnings_insights: BHP FCF estimate by GS (forecast, after dividends and equity investments) for FY27/28/29: at iron ore $95 -2.3bn/0.9bn/-0.2bn, at $85 -3.4/0.2/-0.8, at $75 -4.5/-0.4/-1.5. Copper price not yet flexed.
Glencore has bought about 58% of its $500m buyback (reported progress, not an earnings figure).
BHP Phase 1 Olympic Dam expansion: GS models capex of about US$11bn against the company's last estimate of US$10-11.6bn, with capex peaking near US$3bn p.a. in the early 2030s (GS estimate).

macro_indicators.interpretation: End demand is soft, with only power equipment growing. Apparent demand is held up by scrap shortages, so the underlying weakness is masked.
Air conditioning is over 15% of China copper use, so the swing weighs directly on consumer related copper demand.

macro_indicators.reading: <5% growth YTD, with copper consumption negative y/y
macro_indicators.interpretation: Full year targets suggest some acceleration into year end.

macro_indicators.reading: about 600kt of metal in scrap lost, could reach 1mt by year end
macro_indicators.interpretation: Scrap tightness under the reverse invoice policy supports apparent demand for refined copper.
A forecast cut. BHP free cash flow is weak at current iron ore prices.

risk_factors: US copper tariff decision and a possible Chinese rare earth export ban after the Jan 11 deadline.
Negative US import arbitrage could cut US copper imports from December and send metal back to China.
Weak China end demand in consumer related sectors, including air conditioners and property.
Reverse invoice policy and tax bureau changes affecting scrap supply and copper processing.
BHP free cash flow is negative or near zero through FY29 at current iron ore prices, requiring leverage.
Codelco operational and funding stress in Chile.
Block cave geotechnical and uranium recovery risks at Olympic Dam.
vol_and_positioning: GS commodities desk thinks the macro franchise held a 5/10 short via options coming into the week.
Chinese shorts on SHFE are approaching local highs and were added to on 11/18.
The market has been long or flat copper for two years, similar to gold, so it has room to add.
The copper futures desk points to CTA and related positioning after what the author calls capitulation this week.
China had been selling copper to buy gold. On Monday it sold everything.
geopolitical: US decision on a copper tariff, set against China's possible rare earth export ban with a Jan 11 deadline.
Trump says the US has a rare earth solution. Trump is entering China talks facing an AI supply-chain bottleneck (per Bloomberg).
Rumors of A-share short sale restrictions around the APEC summit, not verified.
China's reverse invoice policy and the tax bureau's stance are tightening scrap supply.
Codelco is in a difficult position in Chile, with the cost of saving El Teniente and a possible sale of El Abra under discussion.

tension_points.bull_case: Apparent demand is supported by scrap tightness. Power equipment is growing and State Grid commitments suggest acceleration into year end. GS sees 2027 as less negative. The market has been long or flat for two years, so there is room to add.
tension_points.bear_case: End demand remains negative at about -2-3% y/y or 500kt. Air conditioner demand fell to -10%, State Grid copper consumption is negative y/y and consumer related sectors are deteriorating.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Signs that the tax bureau steps back from the reverse invoice policy or that supply chain models shift, which would end the scrap tightness supporting apparent demand.

tension_points.theme: us copper tariff vs china rare earths
tension_points.bull_case: The market priced that the US would not tariff copper, which would imply China does not impose a rare earth export ban.
tension_points.bear_case: Trump says the US has a rare earth solution, so the US may keep the copper tariff option. Negative arbitrage will stop US imports from December regardless.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The Jan 11 rare earth export ban deadline, and the pace of Chinese re-exports of copper in December.
